newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Opposition parliamentarians on Tuesday alleged that offices of the two Indian intelligence agencies - The Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) were opened in Bangladesh.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina expected to seek Japanese financial assistance for construction of the proposed Ganges barrage during her scheduled tour to Japan next month.
Parliament on Tuesday adopted an ammendment to its Rules of Procedure providing for non ministers to become chairmen of the House standing committees on ministries.
The government on Tuesday denied the opposition allegation that Indian intelligence agencies had opened office in Bangladesh.
Dhaka's population reached to nine million, Local Government Minister Zillur Rahman told the parliament on Tuesday.
The government has decided to build 2,000 more cyclone shelters in coastal areas.

More than 35 international oil companies have so far procured documents and necessary technical data for participating in the second round of biddings for the country's 15 oil and gas exploration blocks.
The governmet has warned the manpower recruiting agents of stern action if found involved in sending workers to Malaysia illegally. REUTER
